title: Adaptive ingest router and client negotiation playbook for telemetry v2 rollout
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Build and execute a low-risk migration plan for telemetry ingestion that enables multiple schema versions to be routed, transformed, and backfilled without client-side breaking changes. The playbook will coordinate an adaptive ingest router, lightweight client negotiation protocol, and server-side transformation adapters so that SDK/CLI/API clients can gradually opt-in to v2 telemetry while v1 remains supported.

Background: Our analytics pipeline needs a new v2 event envelope to support structured feature-flagging, richer token cost attribution, and deterministic trace IDs. A full cutover will break older SDK/CLI versions and third-party integrations unless we provide server-side negotiation and transformation. Previous tickets have prototyped schema transforms and version adapters; this ticket unifies them into a production-ready rollout plan.

Constraints and non-goals: We must avoid long-lived forks in downstream analytics consumers. This ticket does not include the downstream data-model migrations (e.g., warehouse schema changes) — those will be coordinated but executed in a separate project. We also are not changing client telemetry sampling defaults in this work.

Approach summary:
1) Implement an ingest router that inspects incoming event envelopes for a signed version token or a capability header and routes to one of: passthrough v1 path, v2 validation+ingest, or adaptive-transform service.
2) Publish a minimal negotiation spec for SDK/CLI: a header X-RW-Telemetry-Version + capability bits, fallback semantics, and client-side opt-in flag.
3) Build a set of idempotent transform adapters capable of: adding missing trace fields, renaming fields per v2 mapping, and converting deprecated enum values. Adapters must be replay-safe for backfill.
4) Implement lightweight acceptance tests and canary metrics in staging to validate fidelity and latency impact.
5) Execute a phased rollout: SDK opt-in beta -> client SDK releases with negotiation -> 10% traffic canary via ingest router -> backfill short window for missing attributes -> full rollout -> deprecation notice for v1.

Operational guardrails: latency SLO for ingest router: P95 < 20ms added, error budget for transform failures < 0.1% of events, and monitoring dashboards for transformation failure rate, field-drop rate, and consumer downstream lag.

Deliverables: negotiation spec doc, ingest router implementation, transform adapters, SDK/CLI compatibility PRs, canary dashboard, runbook for rollback and mitigation.
acceptance_criteria: Negotiation spec published and reviewed by SDK/CLI teams
Ingest router deployed to staging with feature-flag gating and a canary knob
Transform adapters validate and convert 99% of test vectors from v1->v2 in staging
Telemetry SDKs can set X-RW-Telemetry-Version and fallback correctly according to spec
Canary metrics (transformation fidelity, added latency, error rate) reported in Grafana with alerts
Rollback runbook documented and tested for at least two failure scenarios
comments: 2026-02-22 | Asha Patel: Kickoff meeting notes attached. We agreed on header-based negotiation to avoid client payload changes. Action: Liam to sketch ingest router API and canary knobs.

2026-02-28 | Liam Ortega: Prototype ingest router implemented as an Envoy Lua filter + lightweight transform service. Initial P95 added latency ~8ms in staging. Posting PR: github.com/redwood/ingest-router/pull/58
2026-03-04 | Priya Nair (SDK): Reviewed negotiation spec. Suggested adding a capability bit for 'prefers-structured-costs' to allow partial opt-ins. Updated spec accordingly.

2026-03-09 | SRE Team: Load test notes - under concurrent 5k req/s, transform path increases CPU on transform workers by ~18%. We need autoscaling policy and circuit breaker defaults before 10% canary.
2026-03-10 | Liam Ortega: Changed canary plan to 5% initially and added a circuit-breaker threshold to the router. Pushing changes to staging for validation.
risks: Downstream consumers may not be able to handle renamed fields without schema migration coordination
Transform adapters introduce latency/regression under burst traffic if autoscaling is not tuned
Client adoption may lag causing prolonged dual-support window and additional maintenance cost
migration_steps: Publish negotiation spec and SDK opt-in instructions
Release SDK/CLI patch with negotiation header support and integration tests
Deploy ingest router to staging behind feature flag
Run transform adapter validation suite with real event snapshots
Enable 5% canary and monitor fidelity and latency for 72 hours
Gradually increase to 25% then 100% with backfill windows and consumer coordination
Schedule deprecation notice and final cutover timeline for v1
notes: Prefer the router-as-a-service model to avoid client-side changes. Keep transforms idempotent and log-only failures for first two weeks of canary. Coordinate with analytics warehouse owners once rollforward fidelity > 99%.
